ca_wall_3.blurb: Wall 3 is the third of five sandstone walls up the canyon behind Arlington Ridge in Santa Barbara, part of the Panic Town crack-climbing zone. All 14 routes are gear climbs apart from one top-rope line, running from about 5.4 to 5.9 and clustering at 5.7 and 5.8. The wall splits into a central tower and two lower flanks, and several lines are two pitches that finish on the tower top, so these are among the longer climbs in the canyon. The tower's stone is a little softer yet still holds gear well. The left flank starts from a shady platform, which keeps it comfortable on warm days. A good first stop for moderate crack climbing.

ca_wall_5.blurb: Wall 5 sits further up the narrow canyon behind Arlington Ridge in Santa Barbara, in the Panic Town group of sandstone walls. It holds 14 routes, nearly all traditional cracks plus a single top-rope line, with grades from about 5.4 to 5.9 and most between 5.7 and 5.8. The dark, hard sandstone offers good protection and some odd, interesting features. Every route starts beneath a cool tree canopy, so an early start suits warm days. Expect to push through vines and poison oak on the way in, and watch for loose blocks coming off the neighbouring wall above.

ca_quarry_the_2.blurb: The Quarry is a small bouldering zone among the Call Box Rocks at Salt Point State Park on the Sonoma coast. It is a low sandstone shelf beside the ocean with 14 problems, ranging from easy V0 to V7. The bulk are V1 and V2 traverses, mantles and liebacks, with a handful of harder V5 to V7 lines for stronger boulderers. It makes a short coastal session rather than a destination day, and the setting is the draw. Walk straight toward the water from the parking pullout; the boulders are hard to spot until you are close. Expect sea air and a left-of-the-arch location.

ca_pixie_rock.blurb: Pixie Rock is a small, very popular formation beside the road at Indian Cove in the northern part of Joshua Tree National Park. The 14 routes are mostly traditional climbs plus four top-rope lines, spanning easy fifth class up to 5.11, with a good number of 5.7 and 5.8 climbs and a few harder 5.10 and 5.11 lines. The approach takes seconds and there is a walk-off at the back, so it suits beginners and families. Many routes face south and get hot, and the busy road setting means company is likely. Cool-season days are the comfortable ones.

ca_upper_poison_dome_south_face.blurb: The south face of Upper Poison Dome is part of the Poison Domes in the Domelands of the Southern Sierra, near Sherman Pass. Climbing here is high-altitude, around 9,000 feet, on polished, featured stone with a tendency toward bold, powerful moves. Of the 14 routes, ten are bolted and four are gear-protected. Grades start near 5.9 and run up to 5.13, with the majority at 5.12. This is a place for confident leaders who like steep, athletic climbing in a remote setting rather than a beginner crag.

ca_back_walls_2.blurb: Back Walls is a section of the Burney Limestone crag, also called The Shredding, in northeast California east of Redding. It has 14 climbs, mostly bolted sport lines with a few gear routes, some top-rope lines and one V3 boulder problem. Grades start around 5.6 and reach 5.12, with many between 5.7 and 5.11. The rock can be dirty and mossy in places. Poison oak is common near the paths. It is a handy spot to add variety to a day on the neighbouring Main Wall.
